themes_detail.label: Sudden Standing Water Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting a localized drainage or flooding emergency in Tottenville/Great Kills that demands immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 standing water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)
Statistical severity rated 'high' with extreme z-score indicating unprecedented spike
Timing aligns with recent winter weather and potential infrastructure strain in district with known sewer gaps per CB budget requests
reporting_angles: Locate the geographic cluster of the 4 complaints; interview affected residents about flooding/pooling water and property damage
Contact DEP about whether this reflects failures in the incomplete sanitary sewer system that CB has requested funding to address for years

themes_detail.label: Illegal Cannabis Retail Boom
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 3 last week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—indicating rapid, possibly unlicensed retail proliferation in the district.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35)
Statistical severity rated 'high' with z-score of 6.35 indicating significant anomaly
Suggests either new storefronts opening or increased community reporting of existing unlicensed operations
reporting_angles: Map the 3 complaints to specific addresses; determine if these are licensed dispensaries or illegal operations and interview neighbors about nuisance concerns
Interview NYPD and state cannabis control board about enforcement activity and compliance in the district

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Violations Escalate
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints surged to 6 last week versus a baseline of 1.8 per week—a 243% spike (z-score: 3.54)—raising questions about restaurant/food vendor safety and inspections in Tottenville/Great Kills.
evidence: 6 food establishment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.54)
Statistical severity rated 'high' with z-score above 3.5 indicating significant deviation
Pattern consistent with seasonal surge or delayed DOHMH inspection backlog surfacing in 311 reports
reporting_angles: Identify the 6 establishments by complaint and interview residents about the violations (sanitation, pests, temperature control, etc.)
Contact DOHMH to determine if there's been a recent inspection wave and whether violations are tied to specific cuisines or establishment types

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 20 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 9.6 per week—a 108% spike (z-score: 3.62)—pointing to acute pavement/trip hazard issues across the district.
evidence: 20 sidewalk condition complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 9.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.62)
Sidewalk repairs align with CB's repeated budget request for street reconstruction via DOT
Complements broader infrastructure strain signals (standing water, maintenance spike)
reporting_angles: Document specific sidewalk hazards (cracked pavement, heaved concrete, tree root damage) with photos and GPS locations
Cross-reference complaints with DOT repair backlog and ask about timeline for addressing known dangerous intersections

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Neglect Spike
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints peaked at 14 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 4.8 per week—a 195% increase (z-score: 4.99)—suggesting systemic upkeep failures at public or commercial facilities.
evidence: 14 maintenance/facility complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.99)
Could reflect NYCHA, DOE, Parks, or other agency facility backlogs
Timing suggests winter-driven heating, pipe, or structural issues
reporting_angles: Obtain the full complaint list to identify whether issues cluster around specific buildings (schools, recreation centers, public housing)
Contact relevant agencies (NYCHA, DOE, Parks) about maintenance staffing and budget constraints during winter months
